Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> Photo Story NDC constituency election records impressive turnout at Bortianor-Ngleshie Amanfro. Source : David Andoh 24 October 2026 5:22pm Audio By Carbonatix
The National Democratic Congress (NDC) constituency executive elections have recorded an impressive turnout at the Bortianor-Ngleshie Amanfro constituency in the Greater Accra Region.
The elections, which started in the early hours of today, are approaching their final stage, with delegates arriving in large numbers to cast their votes.
Voting is taking place at the Astroturf in Tuba, a suburb of Ngleshie Amanfro, where a large crowd of delegates, party supporters, and observers has gathered.
The exercise is being conducted by officials of the Electoral Commission (EC), while members of the party's election committee are coordinating and monitoring the process to ensure a smooth and transparent election.
A number of aspirants are contesting various constituency executive positions, including Chairman, Vice-Chairman, Secretary, Deputy Secretary, Treasurer, Organiser, Deputy Organiser, Communications Officer, Women's Organiser, Deputy Women's Organiser, Youth Organiser, Deputy Youth Organiser and Zongo Caucus Coordinator, in line with the party's structure.
The atmosphere at the venue has been generally calm and orderly, with security personnel present to maintain law and order.
Some delegates who spoke to reporters expressed satisfaction with the conduct of the polls so far, describing the process as peaceful and transparent.
They said the high turnout reflects the enthusiasm of members to elect competent leaders who will strengthen the party at the grassroots level ahead of the 2028 general elections.
Party officials in the constituency said they expect the elections to end peacefully and called on all aspirants and their supporters to accept the outcome in good faith and work together to advance the interest of the NDC in Bortianor-Ngleshie Amanfro.
Counting of ballots is expected to begin immediately after voting ends, with winners to be declared by the Electoral Commission officials.
